r7-attack.title: Attack the pattern
r7-attack.imperative: write plausible regrowth and find what it misses:Write regrowth text a future agent restoring this doctrine would actually write, run it against ENGINE_PLACEHOLDER_RE / CLI_FALLBACK_RE / ENGINE_INVOCATION_RE, and report every miss with the exact string. Judge each miss as a declared limit (observation) or a defeat of the guard's stated purpose (finding).
r7-attack.finding: 27 regrowth strings run against all three patterns; 13 missed. One miss is NOT inside a declared limit and is the finding: a spine-template command line written with any stand-in other than <engine>. 'Second path: <cli> claim --session-id <commander-session-id> --claimed-by commander.' and 'If the door is down: <engine-cli> advance g1 --why ...' and 'Fallback command line: {{engine}} release --session-id <work-id>.' all pass clean. The class matters because a template command line never contains the literal checklist_engine.py, so ENGINE_INVOCATION_RE cannot reach it and the entire class hangs on one 8-char literal; init_work_area.py:24's own comment lists <engine> beside <date>, <N>, <path> as generic prose placeholders it never resolves, so a differently-spelled stand-in is a natural thing for a restoring author to write. Remaining 12 misses fall inside or beside the docstring's declared limits: bare script mention with the verb separated by a blank line or a sentence ('The engine script is checklist_engine.py. To close a gate, advance g1.'); the -m module form ('python3 -m scripts.checklist_engine --file spine.json current'); alias USE where the definition is elsewhere ('Then run $ENGINE claim --session-id <id>'); and command-free paraphrase ('If the door refuses, drive the checklist from a shell with the engine script instead'). Credit where measured: the adjacent-next-line verb form IS caught, Windows backslash paths are caught, absolute installed paths, ./ paths, case and hyphen respellings are caught, and the engine's argparse defines NO short options, so requiring --[A-Za-z] gives up nothing runnable.

r8-predicate-line.title: Judge the invocation predicate's line and whether the test pins it
r8-predicate-line.imperative: Read at least two of the six prose mentions the predicate leaves alone, say whether the line between 'run this from a shell' and 'this file is the engine' is drawn defensibly, and red-proof that TestTheInvocationPredicateItself genuinely pins both directions.
r8-predicate-line.finding: The line is defensible and the test really pins it, with one gap worth naming. Read in full: skills/_shared/global-everyone.md:70 ('The engine's why-capture and refresh primitives (checklist_engine.py, #179)'), :178 ('the engine rail string table (checklist_engine.py, #140)'), :254 ('Nothing enforces the execution-time half in code -- checklist_engine.py does not parse these tags'), and skills/admiral/references/fleet-doctrine.md:234 ('an epic that rewrites checklist_engine.py -- the very engine driving it'). Every one of these names the engine as the COMPONENT that implements or fails to implement a rule; none tells a reader to run anything, and deleting the name from them would make the doctrine unable to say which module it is talking about. Drawing the line at 'tells an agent how to run it' is the right place. Red-proof, done in memory without editing the file: widening the trailing-arg arm from --[A-Za-z] to a bare -- immediately flags the fleet-doctrine em-dash sentence, and dropping the path and trailing-arg arms misses 6 of 6 command shapes -- so both directions genuinely fail when the pattern moves. Independently re-measured on this tree: 16 literal checklist_engine.py occurrences in the walk, 10 caught, 6 left alone, exactly as reported. THE GAP: the closest-to-the-boundary shape in the corpus is not in PROSE_ONLY -- skills/write-a-skill/SKILL.md:20's archetype cell 'a templates/*.json checklist driven through checklist_engine.py', which asserts the DRIVE PATH is the script and is precisely the belief #559 wants removed, yet is left alone (verified) and unpinned. PROSE_ONLY's four strings mirror the rail-table, em-dash, scripts-manifest and does-not-parse shapes and skip this one, so a future widening that starts flagging archetype tables would not be caught by the pin. Where the line sits is the Commander's doctrine call; I report only that the drawn line holds and that its pin has this one hole.

r9-census.title: Re-measure the two reported census discrepancies
r9-census.imperative: Independently re-measure <engine> (10 vs baseline 9) and CLI fallback (16 vs baseline 15) rather than accepting the implementer's arithmetic, and judge whether accepting the CLI-fallback false-alarm class is the right call.
r9-census.finding: Both discrepancies re-measured with my own walk, not the guard's code, and both explanations hold. <engine>: 10 occurrences at 9 addresses. COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json tasks.archive.imperative carries exactly 2 tokens, and sed -n '123p' on that file returns 2 matches, so the baseline's 9 was a LINE count and the extra occurrence is real -- the sweep must edit BOTH tokens on line 123 ('<engine> waive archive --cond c4' and 'CLI fallback: <engine> release'), and a one-edit-per-line sweep leaves one behind. CLI fallback: 16 with the [\\s-] separator, and exactly 15 with a space-only separator -- the delta is one site, skills/workbench/references/checklist-engine.md:45, 'There is no CLI-fallback table below this one', a sentence that forbids the thing while quoting it. My arithmetic reproduces the baseline's 15 exactly, so the baseline was not wrong; the pattern is strictly wider. Accepting that false-alarm class is the right call: a hyphen respelling is the cheapest way to defeat a space-only pattern, so narrowing to duck this one site would trade a real evasion route for one cosmetic red, and the alternative -- a polarity predicate that tries to tell a prohibition from an instruction -- is far more failure-prone than a human reading one line. The site is also lane D2's file, deleted by that lane before g5-final.
